raw_response:
I'm 53, never spent a day in school, but I've farmed these 22.5 mu for 33 years. My father taught me everything I know before he passed, and now it's just me and my wife working the land. Our son is at the factory in Handan six days a week, so he can only help on Sundays. Three mouths to feed, but only two pairs of hands most days.

This year, I'm doing what I always do — no point changing something that keeps us fed. Ten mu goes to wheat and then maize. That's the main system. Wheat goes in around October 10th, same date every year. I use my own saved seed, the best ears from last harvest. Why buy new seed when mine grows fine? Before planting, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the blue-bag kind from the county supply store. In March when the wheat turns green, if it looks yellow and weak, I topdress another half bag of urea. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, and this year should be the same if the rain comes regular. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze-up, once at jointing in March, and once at grain filling in May. Water costs money — the well pump runs on electricity — so I don't water more than I have to.

After we cut the wheat in early June, there's barely a week to get the maize in. I hire Old Wang's tractor to plow fast, then my wife and I plant by hand with the small seeder. Maize has to be hybrid seed, so I buy that from the store — about 50 yuan per mu. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer at planting, and if the leaves look yellow by July, another half bag of urea. Water twice: right after planting, and again when it tassels. If the summer rains are good, maybe I skip the second one. Last year the maize gave me 450 kg per mu.

I keep 5 mu for cotton. It's hard work but the cash is decent. Plant around April 20th. I use local seeds my cousin gave me — not those expensive Bt seeds some people talk about. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then some urea when the flowers come. Water twice, maybe three times if July is scorching. The picking kills us — my wife and I handle what we can, but I hire women from the village for 80 yuan a day to help. Should get about 110 kg of lint per mu if the bolls don't rot.

The rest of the land I split into small plots: 3 mu peanuts, 2.5 mu millet, and 2 mu mung beans. Peanuts go to the oil press and some cash. Millet is for our porridge in winter — we don't sell much. Mung beans are easy; my wife makes mung bean soup in summer. These small plots don't get bought fertilizer — maybe some chicken manure from the neighbor's coop if there's extra. I only water them if I'm already running the pump for wheat or cotton.

Money is always tight. Fertilizer for the whole farm costs about 4,000 yuan. Seeds about 1,000. Electricity for the well pump another 1,500. Hired labor and the tractor plowing about 2,500. Pesticides and herbicides another 500. That's near 9,500 yuan going out before we harvest anything. My wife says her stomach medicine is getting dearer, so I need to keep some cash back. I'd rather apply a little less fertilizer than run out of money if someone gets sick.
